title: Microsoft Teams: QR code images from external senders are blurred by default
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents default QR code blurring, the recipient's reveal action and the absence of an administrator enable or disable control. The external-domain controls, Teams licensing statement and revised rollout window match the sources checked.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Teams blurs images containing QR codes in messages from external senders.
claims.quote: When an external user sends a message that contains an image with a QR code, Teams blurs the image.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The recipient selects Reveal QR code to reveal the image before viewing or scanning it.
claims.quote: Users must explicitly reveal the image before they can view or scan the QR code. Users can select Reveal QR code to view or scan the QR code.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft describes obscuring as precautionary protection encouraging deliberate interaction with QR content that can be used in phishing and fraud.
claims.quote: This precautionary protection helps increase user awareness and encourages more deliberate interaction with QR code content, which can be used in phishing and fraud attempts.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A blurred QR code does not mean Teams determined that the code is malicious, as both Learn and the notice state.
claims.quote: Learn: A blurred QR code doesn't mean that Teams identified the QR code as malicious. MC1470410: The blurred image does not indicate that Microsoft Teams has determined the QR code to be malicious.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Scope: Rollout; controls[0].note
claims.claim: QR code obscuring is enabled by default, correctly represented by defaultState on.
claims.quote: This experience is enabled by default, and there are no admin controls to enable or disable it.

claims.quote: This experience is supported on Teams desktop, web, and mobile clients.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: For users in China on Teams mobile, obscuring applies to QR codes from both internal and external senders.
claims.quote: For users in China on Teams mobile, this experience applies to QR codes in messages sent by both internal and external users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe new data access for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring image detection processing data access autonomous actions other content types. Read the complete QR code obscuring Learn page, roadmap record and MC1470410; none describes new data access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn page does not explain image QR code detection or what happens to images it does not detect.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring image detection processing data access autonomous actions other content types. Read QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams in full; it gives the blur/reveal experience, not a detection algorithm or undetected-image behaviour.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: No autonomous action beyond the described image-display protection is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring image detection processing data access autonomous actions other content types. Read the feature Learn page and MC1470410; neither describes an autonomous action beyond automatically obscuring the image.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each user in the organisation needs a Teams license to use Teams, except when joining Teams meetings anonymously.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The licensing model is included under Teams' existing product-level license requirement, with feature-specific entitlement explicitly unpublished.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license. Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specific to QR code obscuring as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "QR code obscuring" Teams licensing add-on price meter requirements. Read QR code obscuring, Manage Teams licenses and Microsoft Teams add-on licenses; no QR-obscuring-specific entitlement appears in these pages or the returned licensing excerpts.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cost identified by the sources is communication and help desk work, supporting cost low without asserting a published zero price.
claims.quote: Review existing user education materials related to phishing awareness, QR code safety, and external collaboration. Update internal help desk documentation to reflect the new user experience.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No administrator UI or API to enable or disable QR code obscuring is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring protection messages PowerShell Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy Graph admin allowlist disable. Read feature page (no admin controls); searched Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy reference for QR, obscur, blur and phish: no matches.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: external domain row
claims.claim: The Teams admin center route is Users > External access > Teams and Skype for Business users in external organizations > Block only specific external domains > Block external domains.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Users > External access. Next to Teams and Skype for Business users in external organizations, choose Block only specific external domains. Select Block external domains.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: external domain row
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains <domain list> to set the tenant blocked-domain list.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. $list = New-Object Collections.Generic.List[String]; $list.add("contoso.com"); $list.add("fabrikam.com"); Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains $list

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The external-domain row manages the organisation-level domain list for external Teams communication, distinct from user-specific policies.
claims.quote: For meetings and chat with other Microsoft 365 organizations, you can specify which domains you want to trust. By default, all external domains are allowed. You can allow or block certain domains in order to define which organizations your organization trusts for external meetings and chat.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom external access policies can inherit the organisation-level domain list.
claims.quote: Unlike organization settings that apply to everyone, these policies can either inherit the organization's domain list or define completely different domain lists for specific users and groups.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom external access policies can specify a different domain list for assigned users.
claims.quote: Custom policy assigned to user: The value for Allow or block external domains setting in the custom policy takes precedence over organization settings.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The external-domain list is not a control over how a QR code image from an allowed sender is displayed.
claims.quote: When an external user sends a message that contains an image with a QR code, Teams blurs the image. This experience is enabled by default, and there are no admin controls to enable or disable it.

claims.where: Scope: Out of scope
claims.claim: The QR code obscuring Learn page does not describe protection for other content types.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring image detection processing data access autonomous actions other content types. Read the complete QR code obscuring page; it describes images containing QR codes in Teams messages, not other content types.

claims.where: Open questions: trusted-sender allow list
claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator allow list for trusted external senders or domains is documented for QR code obscuring.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring protection messages PowerShell Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy Graph admin allowlist disable. Read QR code obscuring and external-access Learn pages; no QR-specific allow list is documented, and general domain lists govern communication.
